summary.headline: Knack Packaging Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 52.5% to INR294.76 crores, but EBITDA margin fell 285 bps to 16.35% on polymer cost pass-through lag.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations reached a record INR294.76 crores in Q2 FY27 (up 52.5% YoY), with EBITDA up 29.9% to INR49.77 crores but margin down 285 bps to 16.35%. Management attributed the margin squeeze to polypropylene prices rising over 50% within weeks after the West Asia conflict, plus higher Red Sea freight costs, with price pass-through lagging by one to two quarters. PAT rose 21.2% to INR25.02 crores, though it absorbed a INR2.62 crores share of loss from the Sayem Knack JV in Mexico. Management expects margin recovery from Q3 FY27 as price revisions flow through, subject to market stabilisation.

financial_highlights.change: Moderation attributed to post-IPO capital base
Down from INR39 crores (as stated by analyst)

segments.name: Packaging (bags, PLWPP and pinch-bottom)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 volume was 11,252 metric tons, up 3% QoQ from 10,940 MT and up about 13-14% YoY from 9,927 MT. Pinch-bottom bags contribute about 21% of revenue, and PLWPP is about 71-72% of volume.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Sold to 75 countries across 6 continents as of September 2026, up from 74 at end Q1 FY27 and 71 in FY26. Export receivable cycles are longer than domestic, adding to working capital.

segments.name: Sayem Knack JV (Mexico)
segments.commentary: Greenfield plant with 400 MT installed capacity; selling about 80 MT/month last quarter, targeting 100-120 MT in Q3. Breakeven estimated at about 120 MT/month; JV loss was INR6.06 crores in H1 and INR2.62 crores in Q2.

guidance_outlook: Margin expected to recover from Q3 FY27 as price revisions flow through, subject to market stabilisation; management said full loss recovery in one quarter is difficult.
Volume expected to be better in Q3 than Q2, with new capacity (5,040 MT added in August 2026) ramping to about 50% utilisation (about 2,500 MT).
Mexico JV expected to reach breakeven in Q3 FY27, with Q4 as the committed-target fallback.
Management said full-year targets are on track, though Q2 is significantly down.
Expansion targeted for October 2027, taking installed capacity to about 69,000-72,000 MT from about 42,000 MT.
Pinch-bottom output targeted at 25,000-30,000 MT, with 2 new pinch machines due around October 2027 and full benefit by 2028.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity is about 42,000 MT per year; running at about 39,000-40,000 MT effective, with utilisation at 90-91%.
5,040 MT of new capacity added in August 2026, ramping up; a rented plant added about two months before the call is expected to add capacity in one to two months.

Pinch-bottom: 5 machines in place, 2 added in Q4 FY26 (March 2026) still ramping; pinch-bottom machine utilisation about 60-70%. Two more pinch machines have 1-1.5 year lead time, targeted for October 2027.
Expansion (new Gujarat plant) targeted for October 2027 and cited as a key milestone through 2027.
Mexico JV: 400 MT installed capacity, utilised at about 80-90 MT/month.
demand_pricing: Polypropylene prices rose more than 50% within weeks of the West Asia conflict and stayed elevated through Q2; management cited polymer moving from about INR92 pre-war to INR160 at peak.

About 45-50% of customers are on conversion-cost contracts where bag prices move with polymer; the rest are order-by-order. Management said price hikes of 25-30% were applied immediately, with realisation lag of 1-2 quarters.
Management said gross margin impact was about 7% from the price lag; raw material rose about 26% in the quarter.
EBITDA per kg fell to about INR45 in Q2 from about INR54-55 in Q1 (per management; analyst cited INR36 vs INR51-52, which management confirmed as directionally correct).
New INR150 crore per year, 3-year contract renewal with a large US-based pet food and animal nutrition packaging customer, announced 2 October 2026; minimum INR150 crores per year.
Demand drivers cited: pet food (double-digit growth in India), rice (pinch-bottom season starting), and migration from jute, paper and POPP bags to PLWPP and pinch-bottom.

qa_highlights.question: What volume growth was achieved in Q2, and what is plant utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was 11,252 MT, up 3% QoQ and about 13-14% YoY; plant utilisation is about 90-91%, with 5,040 MT of capacity added in August.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike was taken in Q2 and what is planned for Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw material rose about 26%, gross margin impact was about 7%, and the remaining increase was passed on with the bulk expected to reflect in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin on track to recover in Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q3 and Q4 to be better in volume and margin, but said full recovery depends on the market and crude prices; 99% of the cost increase is expected to be covered.

qa_highlights.question: How scalable is the INR150 crore international order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a minimum INR150 crore per year contract for 3 years from an existing US customer, with scope to add products, with the customer currently serving 8-9 countries against more than 100 for the customer.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating cash flow fall in H1 and is it seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said inventory rose by about INR26.9 crores due to scale-up, and export receivables added about INR55 crores; tax was higher with effective rate about 25%, plus deferred tax and IPO-related items.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Mexico JV break even and what is its capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Installed capacity is 400 MT/month; sales were about 80 MT last quarter, targeted at 100-120 MT in Q3, with breakeven around 120 MT/month and Q3 expected to be near breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: Will the lost margin be recovered, and should pinch-bottom margins be higher YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full recovery in one quarter is difficult; Q3 is expected to recover a small part. Management agreed that with five pinch machines vs three last year, pinch-bottom margins should be higher YoY.

risks_watch: Polymer and crude price volatility: management said the 1% of residual risk depends on the market, and the price lag of 1-2 quarters could hurt margins again.
Mexico JV losses weigh on consolidated PAT until breakeven; Q1 and Q2 losses were INR6.06 crores in H1 and INR2.62 crores in Q2.
Working-capital build from exports (longer receivable cycles) and inventory; H1 operating cash flow fell to INR22 crores from INR39 crores.
Pinch-bottom market size and ability to convert PLWPP customers; pinch-bottom utilisation only about 60-70% after new machines.
Expansion timeline: October 2027 is the deadline for the new Gujarat expansion, and any slippage would limit volume growth.
Concentration: the INR150 crore contract is a large single-customer renewal; the 45-50% contracted book is also seasonal.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term volume and capacity, but cautious and somewhat hedged on near-term margin recovery, repeatedly qualifying Q3 outcomes with market and crude-price dependence. Management was also less precise on some figures during Q&A, including per-kg EBITDA and the Mexico breakeven timeline, which were revised within the call.
key_quotes: Quarter 2 FY27 was a stable and strong growth for Knack Packaging.
Our priority is to restore our EBITDA margin as pricing adjustments flow through from Quarter 3 FY27 and then to improve it further by increasing the share of value-added products.
So, this is a INR150 crores every month order, every year order. It is a 1-year minimum, it is a minimum INR150 crores.
There is no doubt on the yearly achievement. Yes, this quarter is a significant little bit down, but yearly our target is, we are on the track.

adds.what: 5,040 MT/yr new capacity added August 2026, ramping to ~50% utilisation (~2,500 MT)
Rented plant added ~2 months before call, expected to add capacity in 1-2 months
2 pinch-bottom machines (1-1.5 yr lead time), targeted October 2027

growth.why: Management guides margin recovery from Q3 FY27 and says full-year targets are on track; backing is partial: 5,040 MT added Aug 2026 ramping, rented plant coming in 1-2 months, a INR150 crore/yr 3-year US pet food contract renewal, and Gujarat expansion (~42,000 to ~69,000-72,000 MT) targeted October 2027, which is about 4 quarters out. No explicit revenue growth % guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin recovery from Q3 FY27 as 25-30% price hikes flow through, but 1-2 quarter pass-through lag and a 7% gross-margin hit mean only a small part recovers in Q3 (vs 16.35% Q2 margin, 19.25% a year ago).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Aug 2026 done; Q1 FY28 rented plant; Oct 2027 Gujarat
rows.why: 5,040 MT added Aug 2026 is already live and a rented plant is due in 1-2 months; Gujarat expansion takes capacity from ~42,000 to ~69,000-72,000 MT with an October 2027 deadline, about 4 quarters out.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Volume was 11,252 MT in Q2 (+3% QoQ, +13-14% YoY) at 90-91% utilisation, and management expects Q3 volume better than Q2 as the 5,040 MT ramps toward ~2,500 MT (~50%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 90-91% with the Gujarat expansion not due until October 2027, so further capacity announcements are probable given high utilisation.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said full-year targets are on track but only hedged on Q3 margin; Q2 is significantly down and no revenue growth % was guided, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin fell 285 bps to 16.35% and management said full loss recovery in one quarter is difficult, with the outcome dependent on crude and polymer prices and a 1-2 quarter lag.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pinch-bottom output targeted at 25,000-30,000 MT with 2 more machines due October 2027, but these are capacity additions rather than discrete new products; no new product launch was named.

rows.label: INR150 crore/yr 3-year US pet food contract renewal
rows.why: Minimum INR150 crores per year for 3 years from an existing US customer, announced 2 October 2026, adds a firm revenue floor against H1 revenue of INR569.11 crores.

rows.label: Sayem Knack Mexico JV breakeven
rows.why: JV losses were INR6.06 crores in H1 and INR2.62 crores in Q2 at about 80 MT/month sales against ~120 MT/month breakeven, with 100-120 MT targeted for Q3 and Q4 only as the committed fallback.

rows.label: Export footprint expansion
rows.why: Sold to 75 countries as of Sept 2026 (74 at end Q1 FY27, 71 in FY26), but export receivables added about INR55 crores in H1, so growth ties up working capital.

tone.note: Management was confident on capacity, the INR150 crore contract and the October 2027 Gujarat expansion, but cautious and hedged on Q3 margin recovery given crude and polymer dependence; analysts pushed on per-kg EBITDA, the Mexico breakeven timeline, and the H1 operating cash flow drop.
